stories.headline: US-bound flights out of Australia delayed after telecommunications outage grounded American planes
stories.summary: A telecommunications outage prompted US air traffic control authorities to ground all departing flights nationwide, causing delays that extended to Australian airports with US-bound services. The FAA lifted the ground stop hours later, though recovery across the system remained incomplete as airports worked to clear backlogs.

stories.headline: Microsoft ‘deeply sorry’ for global outage that could have billion-dollar impact on Australia
stories.summary: A faulty security update from third-party software provider CrowdStrike caused Microsoft services including Outlook and Teams to go offline globally, potentially costing Australia's economy over a billion dollars in disrupted business operations. Microsoft has restored all services and stated the outage resulted from neither a cyberattack nor artificial intelligence malfunction.

stories.headline: US has floated Ukraine ceding Donbas for Nato membership, Zelensky says
stories.summary: U.S. officials have privately suggested that Ukraine might gain NATO membership in exchange for ceding the Donbas region to Russia, according to President Zelensky's account of ongoing discussions. European leaders are preparing coordinated positions for potential peace negotiations while warning that Russia continues to complicate talks with bad-faith proposals.

stories.headline: Trump, Putin and Xi plan historic joint meeting in China next week, White House says
stories.summary: Trump, Putin, and Xi plan to hold their first trilateral meeting in China next week, with nuclear arms control emerging as a key discussion point. The three leaders will gather amid heightened global tensions over weapons proliferation and shifting geopolitical alignments.

stories.headline: Watch: Cruise ship overturns after collision with tanker in New Orleans
stories.summary: A tanker collided with a cruise ship on the Mississippi River near New Orleans, causing the cruise ship to overturn in the waterway. All passengers and crew members were evacuated safely, though 32 people received hospital treatment for injuries sustained in the incident.

stories.headline: Nearly $20m found in Hungary’s forests, buildings amid corruption probe
stories.summary: Hungarian authorities have recovered approximately $20 million in cash discovered hidden in forests and buildings as part of an ongoing corruption investigation involving a former government official. The discovery suggests efforts to conceal assets during a graft inquiry that implicates figures close to Prime Minister Viktor Orbán's administration.

stories.headline: South Sudan postpones first-ever national elections until February
stories.summary: South Sudan postpones its inaugural national elections to February 2027, extending the timeline for holding votes originally scheduled for an earlier date. The delay affects a country working to establish democratic processes after years of conflict, with voter registration already underway in preparation for the elections.

stories.headline: Qatar and Turkiye sign a mutual defence pact: What do we know?
stories.summary: Qatar and Türkiye have signed a mutual defence agreement that commits both nations to coordinate militarily and diplomatically in response to external threats. The pact reflects deepening strategic ties between the two countries and positions them as aligned partners in regional security matters.

stories.headline: Pochettino bids emotional farewell to US football ahead of Man Utd move
stories.summary: Mauricio Pochettino departs his role with the US national team to become Manchester United's new manager. His exit marks the end of a significant tenure in American soccer and represents a notable managerial change for one of English football's largest clubs.
